title: I'm a teacher and used AI for a educational game prototype
author: tildareads
selftext:
I'm a primary school teacher so obviously I won't introduce myself as a game developer, but with all this noise around AI, I wanted to explore how I could use to teach art history with my kids.

I used fable 5.2 to create a side-scrolling platformer where the levels are real paintings. Each one teaches its own technique: blow ochre through a hollow bone, lay six glazes until the Mona Lisa rises out of the underdrawing, etc

The music score is ten instrument palettes synthesised: they crossfade by how close you are to each painting, through a generated convolution reverb.

The ambition is not teach art history the way a museum does (they will do it much better) but trying to familiarize a kid's eye with different aesthetics and the techniques behind them.

I would love your feedback and learn from your expertise on how to make it an actual game and not a prototype.

comments.author: chwh_dev
comments.body: I think the idea behind your game is really meaningful. I hope it helps a lot of people. If you have the time, it might be nice to try a mix of close-ups and wider shots so players can see each technique up close and then see how it fits into the whole painting.

replies.author: tildareads
replies.body: atm the full painting is visible with a fact about the artwork at the end of each level when you are done with the associated technique

comments.author: pixelvspixel
comments.body:
I think this is a great idea and a pretty decent start to the execution. I know it’s just for your kids. But some polish could go a long way.

\- Try some parallax effects with your layouts  
Perhaps some small puppet warps on characters in paintings.  Some small motion moments like the woman pouring water from the jug.  
\-Character feels a bit stiff in their locomotion  
\- I like that you went minimal and modern on the little UI there is

Cheers!

replies.author: tildareads
replies.body: Amazing ideas. I really see how these motions could bring more immersion feeling with sound as well. Will work on this!

replies.author: pixelvspixel
replies.body: For sure. Feel free to DM, I spent several years in professional EDtech software once upon a time.

replies.author: darkoblivion000
replies.body:
A parallax effect would really give another dimension to classic art. Unless you perceive that to be a bastardizatipn of the art. I say that unironically because you or someone could for sure.

A few years ago I went to a Van Gogh exhibit down by Atlantic City. They had huge rooms where they took a few of his paintings and you stood or sat and basically were immersed as his painting came to life - the streetlights shined and people moves and the paint itself wavered and flowed and that was an amazing experience for me.

I think a parallax effect and or slight animation effect to objects that should be moving or flowing could really bring things to life

comments.author: Briskfall
comments.body:
It's legit cool and lowers friction to different styles.

You said that you wanted them to "familiarise" with the tech behind, so why not a "how to draw/recreate" part? Though that might make the scope expand a whole lot.

replies.author: tildareads
replies.body: That is a big challenge but I think this is where I should be aiming at

comments.author: johnesco
comments.body:
My vision of educators with access to AI with which to make software at will:

Year 2090: Ok class, the grades on the history of the battle of Battle of Hastings were abysmal so we are going to study it again. Put on your VR glasses and we're going to back to where King Harold’s infantry holds the crest and slope of Senlac Hill, and those who want to play William’s army join on group 2.

replies.author: tildareads
replies.body: Those who don’t behave properly will assist from the enemy lines

comments.body:
Looks good man

What did you do to get good animation like that?

replies.body: Lots of credits and lots of trials

replies.body: Like jsut fable 5.2 or claude code credits? Or outside dedicated art AI platforms?

comments.author: Song-Historical
comments.body: Yeah I love it. This is the sort of thing this tech should enable, people who would otherwise never consider making something doing so. Reminds me of the ambition that educational games when I was young had.

replies.author: tildareads
replies.body: We need to believe that this tech is a CRAZY enabler

replies.author: Song-Historical
replies.body: I remember cereal boxes coming with weird educational games on cd way back in the day.

comments.author: chaylarian
comments.body: This is one of the best uses of AI I've seen for a long while

comments.author: Comet7777
comments.body: This is seriously one of the coolest applications of all of this AI game dev stuff. OP I hope you don’t mind if I share it in a YouTube series of good AI games?

replies.author: tildareads
replies.body: Thank you so much ! Happy to share any context and behind the scenes!
